title: Brightloom Analytics adds machine learning to retail forecasting
text: Brightloom Analytics said on Thursday that its retail forecasting software now uses machine learning models trained on five years of store sales. The company said early customers in Millbrook cut unsold stock by a tenth. Chief executive Dana Whitlock said artificial intelligence would be built into every product the firm sells by next year.

title: Ninefold Bank shares rise after quarterly results
text: Shares of Ninefold Bank rose four percent on the regional stock exchange after the lender reported higher lending income for the fourth quarter. Analysts said the bank's cost cutting had begun to show, though its mortgage book grew more slowly than those of its rivals.

title: Port Halden council approves new ferry terminal
text: The Port Halden council voted seven to two on Tuesday to approve a new ferry terminal on the north quay. Construction is expected to begin in the spring and to create about two hundred jobs. Opponents argued the plan would add traffic to Harbour Road.

title: Gulls beat Foxes in season opener
text: The Port Halden Gulls opened the season with a 3-1 win over the Millbrook Foxes in front of a sold-out crowd. Striker Marco Ellery scored twice in the second half, and coach Irene Vasquez praised the team's defensive shape.

title: Kestrel Robotics opens warehouse automation lab
text: Kestrel Robotics opened a research lab in Eastvale to develop robots that pick and pack orders in warehouses. The company plans to hire sixty engineers over two years and to test its machines with Quarry Bay Logistics.

title: Chatbots handle a third of customer service calls at Orchard Health
text: Orchard Health said automated assistants built on artificial intelligence now answer a third of the questions its customers ask by phone and chat. The insurer said human agents were moved to complex claims rather than laid off, and that waiting times fell by half.

title: Millbrook library extends weekend hours
text: The Millbrook public library will open on Sundays from April after the town approved extra funding. Librarian Teresa Gow said demand for its computer classes and children's reading groups had grown every year since 2014.

title: Storm brings flooding to coastal towns
text: Heavy rain and high tides flooded streets in Port Halden and nearby coastal villages overnight. Emergency services evacuated forty homes, and the weather service warned of more rain through the weekend.

title: Stock market ends week higher on technology gains
text: The regional stock market index closed the week up two percent, led by technology companies. Kestrel Robotics and Brightloom Analytics were among the biggest gainers, while energy shares fell as oil prices slipped.

title: AI hiring tools draw scrutiny from regulators
text: Regulators said they would review software that uses artificial intelligence to screen job applicants, after complaints that some tools ranked candidates unfairly. Employers in the region increasingly use such systems to sort thousands of applications for each opening.

title: Eastvale Rovers sign veteran goalkeeper
text: The Eastvale Rovers signed goalkeeper Tomas Brandt on a one-year contract. Brandt, 34, played ten seasons for the Port Halden Gulls and will compete for the starting place with the younger keeper Leo Marsh.

title: Quarry Bay Logistics to expand port operations
text: Quarry Bay Logistics will lease two more berths at the Port Halden container terminal, the company said. The expansion is expected to add one hundred and twenty jobs, mostly for crane operators and drivers.

title: Tidewater Energy profit falls as wind projects are delayed
text: Tidewater Energy reported a drop in first-quarter profit after delays to two offshore wind projects. The company kept its full-year forecast and said the turbines would be connected to the grid by autumn.

title: Banks turn to machine learning to spot fraud
text: Ninefold Bank and other lenders are using machine learning to flag suspicious card payments within seconds. The bank said the system catches more fraud than its old rules while sending fewer false alerts to customers.

title: Larkspur Foods opens bakery in Millbrook
text: Larkspur Foods opened a bakery on Main Street in Millbrook, its fifth in the valley. The company said it hired twenty-five local workers and buys its flour from mills in the region.

title: Foxes reach cup semifinal
text: The Millbrook Foxes reached the regional cup semifinal with a 2-0 win over the Eastvale Rovers. Midfielder Aisha Coleman scored the opening goal from a free kick, and the Foxes kept their fourth clean sheet in a row.

title: Heat wave strains power grid
text: Temperatures above thirty-five degrees pushed electricity demand to a record, and Tidewater Energy asked businesses to cut use during the afternoon peak. Hospitals in the region said they had treated dozens of people for heat exhaustion.

title: Retailers report strong summer sales
text: Retailers across the valley reported their best summer sales in five years, helped by warm weather and tourism. Larkspur Foods and other customers of Brightloom Analytics cited better stock planning as a reason for fewer empty shelves.

title: Kestrel Robotics raises funds for delivery robots
text: Kestrel Robotics raised forty million in new funding to build small robots that deliver parcels on pavements. The company will begin trials in Eastvale this winter and said the robots use artificial intelligence to avoid pedestrians.

title: Port Halden marks two hundred years of its harbour
text: Port Halden celebrated the two hundredth anniversary of its harbour with a parade of tall ships. Mayor Lucia Ferrante unveiled a plaque on the north quay where the first pier was built.

title: Gulls win regional cup
text: The Port Halden Gulls won the regional cup with a 1-0 victory over the Millbrook Foxes. Marco Ellery scored the only goal in extra time and finished the season as the league's top scorer.

title: Unemployment falls to six-year low
text: Unemployment in the region fell to its lowest level in six years, according to new figures. Hiring was strongest in logistics, health care and technology, while the number of manufacturing jobs was flat.

title: Orchard Health uses AI to read medical scans
text: Orchard Health began a pilot in which software using artificial intelligence reviews X-ray images before a radiologist does. The insurer said the tool puts urgent cases first and does not replace the judgment of doctors.

title: Millbrook schools add coding classes
text: Every secondary school in Millbrook will teach programming from next year, the school board said. The courses were designed with Brightloom Analytics, which will also offer summer internships to students.

title: Eastvale bridge reopens after repairs
text: The Eastvale river bridge reopened to traffic after eight months of repairs. Drivers had faced detours of up to forty minutes, and local shops said business suffered during the closure.

title: Ninefold Bank to cut branches as customers move online
text: Ninefold Bank will close twelve branches next year as more customers bank on their phones. The bank said staff would be offered roles in its call centres and in its new digital services team.

title: Rovers appoint new coach
text: The Eastvale Rovers named the former defender Grace Okoye as head coach after a disappointing season. Okoye said she would focus on young players from the club's academy.

title: Companies struggle to hire data scientists
text: Firms in the region say they cannot find enough data scientists and machine learning engineers. Brightloom Analytics and Kestrel Robotics have raised salaries and opened offices closer to the university to attract graduates.

title: Ferry terminal construction begins
text: Work began on the new Port Halden ferry terminal, with cranes from Quarry Bay Logistics lifting the first steel frames into place. The terminal is due to open in 2019.

title: Stock market closes year up eleven percent
text: The regional stock market finished the year eleven percent higher, its best year since 2013. Technology and logistics companies led the gains, and investors expect interest rates to rise slowly next year.

title: Snowstorm closes roads and schools
text: A heavy snowstorm closed schools in Millbrook and Eastvale and left hundreds of drivers stranded on the valley highway. Crews worked overnight to clear the main roads.

title: Retail chain tests cashier-free stores
text: Larkspur Foods is testing a store in Port Halden where shoppers pay without a cashier. Cameras and sensors track the items taken from shelves, and the company said artificial intelligence matches each item to the shopper's account.

title: Ellery signs new contract with Gulls
text: Striker Marco Ellery signed a three-year contract extension with the Port Halden Gulls. The club said the deal keeps its top scorer in Port Halden through 2020.

title: Quarry Bay Logistics reports record volumes
text: Quarry Bay Logistics handled a record number of containers last year, helped by online shopping. The company said its warehouse robots from Kestrel Robotics cut the time to fill an order by a third.

title: Millbrook farmers market moves indoors
text: The Millbrook farmers market will move into the old textile mill for the winter months. Organisers said more than forty stalls had signed up, including one run by Larkspur Foods.

title: Brightloom Analytics launches AI assistant for small businesses
text: Brightloom Analytics launched an assistant that answers questions about sales, stock and staffing for small businesses. Owners ask questions in plain language, and the software uses artificial intelligence to turn them into reports.

title: River cleanup volunteers collect two tonnes of waste
text: Volunteers collected two tonnes of litter from the Eastvale river during a weekend cleanup. The town council said it would add bins along the riverside path.

title: Interest rate rise lifts bank shares
text: The central bank raised interest rates by a quarter point, and Ninefold Bank shares rose three percent on the stock market. Mortgage borrowers will pay more from next month.

title: Foxes win league title
text: The Millbrook Foxes won their first league title in twenty years after a 2-2 draw with the Port Halden Gulls on the final day. Aisha Coleman was named player of the season.

title: Automation reshapes warehouse jobs
text: As warehouses add robots, workers are moving from picking goods to supervising machines and repairing them. Quarry Bay Logistics said it had retrained two hundred staff and that its total employment had grown.

title: Port Halden hosts sailing regatta
text: More than one hundred boats raced in the Port Halden regatta, the largest in its history. Hotels reported full bookings, and the council said the event brought visitors from across the country.

title: Tidewater Energy connects offshore wind farm
text: Tidewater Energy connected its first offshore wind farm to the grid, enough to power sixty thousand homes. Its shares rose two percent on the stock market after the announcement.

title: Millbrook hospital opens new wing
text: Millbrook General Hospital opened a new wing with forty beds and a children's ward. Orchard Health contributed to the cost and will use the wing for a trial of remote patient monitoring.

title: Orchard Health expands AI triage
text: Orchard Health extended its artificial intelligence triage tool to all its clinics after the pilot cut waiting times. Doctors said the software helps them see the most urgent patients first.

title: Rovers start season in new stadium
text: The Eastvale Rovers played their first match at their new stadium, beating the Millbrook Foxes 2-1. Coach Grace Okoye gave debuts to three players from the academy.

title: Drought prompts water restrictions
text: The water authority banned garden hoses in Millbrook and Eastvale after the driest summer on record. Farmers said crop yields would fall, and Larkspur Foods warned of higher bread prices.

title: Kestrel Robotics plans stock market listing
text: Kestrel Robotics said it plans to list its shares on the regional stock exchange next year. The company makes warehouse and delivery robots and has hired more than three hundred people since 2016.

title: Survey: most firms now use artificial intelligence
text: A survey of businesses in the region found that most now use artificial intelligence in at least one area, most often customer service, forecasting and fraud detection. Smaller firms said cost and a lack of skilled staff held them back.

title: Ferry terminal opens early
text: The new Port Halden ferry terminal opened two months ahead of schedule. Mayor Lucia Ferrante said the terminal would double the number of daily crossings to the islands.

title: Job openings in technology reach record
text: Job openings for software engineers and data analysts reached a record in December. Employers including Brightloom Analytics, Kestrel Robotics and Ninefold Bank said hiring for artificial intelligence skills was their top priority for next year.
